sentences.text:
The Land Acquisition ... vs R.Raghunath Reddy on 4 October,
2024
Author: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili  HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE ABHINAND KUMAR SHAVILI  AND  HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE LAXMI NARAYANA ALISHETTY  LAAS.No.369 of 2014 JUDGMENT:
(per Hon'ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty) Heard learned Government Pleader for Appeals appearing for the appellant-Land Acquisition Officer.
Though Sri K.Sreedhar Rao, advocate, is on record for the respondents/claimants, none appeared to make submissions on behalf of the respondents/claimants.

2. This appeal, under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, (for short 'the Act') is filed by the Land Acquisition Officer, Mahabubnagar, aggrieved by the common order and decree dated 29.09.2005 passed in respect of OP.No.73 of 1994 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge,
Mahabubnagar (hereinafter referred to as "the Reference Court').
3.

The facts of the case, briefly stated, are that lands totally admeasuring Acs.6.04 guntas in Sy.Nos.8/2, 13/2, 14/2, 15/2 16/2, 21/2, 23/2, 100/2, 105/2 and 106 situated within the limits of Kothur Village and Mandal, Mahabubnagar District, which includes the land belonging to the respondents herein/claimants, 2 AKS, J & LNA, J were acquired for construction of railway over bridge at Kothur Village; that the Draft Notification under Section 4(1) of the Act was published in the official Gazette on 11.02.1991; that draft notification under Section 6 of the Act was also published in the official gazette; that prior to that, possession of the subject lands was taken by the Requisition authority on 24.09.1989; and that after following the procedure prescribed under the Act, the Land Acquisition Officer passed an Award, dated 20.07.1993, fixing the market value of the subject acquired lands @ Rs.10/- per square yard.
4. Not being satisfied with the compensation granted by the Land Acquisition Officer, the respondents/claimants sought reference under Section 18 of the Act and the same was referred to the competent civil Court and numbered as O.P.No.73 of 1994 on the file of the Reference Court.
Subsequently, the said O.P. was tried along with a batch of O.Ps., viz., O.P.Nos.71, 72, 75, 76, 81 and 92 of 1994, wherein common evidence was adduced.
5. Before the Reference Court, in the joint trial, on behalf of the claimants, P.Ws-1 to 3 were examined and Exs.A-1 to A-8 3 AKS, J & LNA, J were marked.

On behalf of the Referring Officer,
The Land Acquisition ... vs R.Raghunath Reddy on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46845184/
1 RW-1 was examined and Ex.B-1-Award was marked.

6. The Reference Court, on appreciation of the evidence, both oral and documentary, placed on record, passed common order enhancing the market value of the acquired lands to Rs.100/- per square yard from Rs.10/- per square yard as was awarded by the Land Acquisition Officer.

Challenging the said common order, the present appeal is filed in respect of the order passed in LAOP.No.73 of 1994.
7.

It is contended by the learned Government Pleader for Appeals appearing for the appellant that the Land Acquisition Officer has referred to as many as 222 registered sale transactions relating to three years preceding the date of 4(1) notification and after analyzing the same with regard to the nature of soil, location and similarities of the lands thereunder to that of the acquired lands, rightly fixed the market value of the acquired lands; that the Reference Court without appreciating the evidence on record and the reasons assigned by the Land Acquisition Officer in Ex.B-1- Award, erred in enhancing the market value of the acquired lands 4 AKS, J & LNA, J by ten times; and that therefore, the impugned order is liable to be set aside.

8. In order to fix fair and reasonable market value of the subject acquired lands, this Court has scrupulously perused the entire evidence, both oral and documentary, placed on record, the impugned order as well as Ex.B-1-Award passed by the Land Acquisition Officer.

9. P.Ws.1 and 2 are the claimants in the batch of O.Ps and they deposed reiterating their case as stated in their claim petitions to the effect that the subject acquired lands are located on NH-7 leading from Hyderabad to Bangalore via Kurnool and as such, the said lands have great commercial value; that the Government offices like MRO's Office, etc., are at a distance of  km and number of hostels, restaurants, etc., are very near to the subject acquired lands; that the lands at Kothur village were sold on yardage basis even prior to the date of 4(1) notification; that the market value of the lands in the vicinity of the subject acquired lands is ranging from Rs.54 to Rs.158/- per square yard;
and that the Land Acquisition Officer though discussed 222 sale 5 AKS, J & LNA, J transactions, has not arrived at correct market value of the acquired lands.
10 . P.W-3 deposed that in the year 1999, he sold land to an extent of 240 square yards in Sy.No.40/A @ Rs.150/- per square yard.
In the instant case, 4(1) notification was issued in the year 1991 and the Award was passed by the Land Acquisition Officer in the year 1993.

The evidence of P.W-3 regarding sale of land relates to post-notification, that too, eight years after issuance of 4(1)
notification and hence, the same cannot be taken into consideration and it is not helpful to the claimants.
11. In the joint trial, on behalf of the claimants, Exs.A-2 to A-8- sale deeds were got marked.

In fact,
in the Award, while referring to and analyzing the sale statistics, the Land Acquisition Officer has also referred to Exs.A-2 to A-4-registered sale deeds, however, discarded the same.

12. The Reference Court has minutely perused and analyzed the Award and has taken note of the fact that the market value of the lands covered in the sale statistics collected and referred to by the The Land Acquisition ... vs R.Raghunath Reddy on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46845184/
2

Land Acquisition Officer in Ex.B-1-Award shows that huge 6 AKS, J & LNA, J number of sale transactions took place in Kothur Village on yardage basis and hence, the Reference Court observed that there is great demand for land at Kothur on yardage basis.

The Reference Court further observed that the market value reflected in the said sale transactions referred to in Ex.B-1-Award was ranging from Rs.65/- per square yard to Rs.158/- per square yard.
13.

As regards the exhibits, i.e., Exs.A-6 and A-7, it is to be noted that Ex.A-6 is registered sale deed dated 12.05.1994 i.e., it relates to post-notification and Ex.A-7-Award is dated 20.01.1998, i.e., it is passed after nearly four years from the date of passing of Ex.B-1-Award and therefore, the said exhibits cannot be considered for determining the market value of the acquired lands.
14.
This Court on perusal of Ex.B-1-Award concurs with the above findings of the Reference Court.
Further, it is to be noted that the sale transactions covered under Exs.A-2 to A-4 were referred to by the Land Acquisition Officer in Ex.B-1-Award.
The rate per square yard of land as reflected in Exs.A-2 to A-4 is Rs.158/-, Rs.117 and Rs.101/- respectively.

Therefore, the highest market value is reflected under Ex.A-2-sale deed which is Rs.158/-
7 AKS, J & LNA, J per square yard.

However, it is to be seen that Ex.A-2-sale deed is dated 18.02.1991, i.e. after publication of 4(1) notification on 11.02.1991 and hence, the same cannot be taken into consideration for fixation of fair market value of the subject acquired lands.
15. Even if the average sale value under Exs.A-2 to A-4 is taken, it comes to Rs.151/- per square yard.

Therefore, in this regard, the contention of the learned Government Pleader that the value of lands as per the sale statistics collected by the Land Acquisition Officer is ranging from Rs.5/- to Rs.15/-
per square yard is incorrect and has no basis.
16. If 1/3rd of the above assessed value is deducted towards developmental charges, the same comes to Rs.100/- per square yard, as was rightly fixed by the Reference Court.

17. In the light of the foregoing reasons, the appellant miserably failed to show any illegality or irregularity committed by the Reference Court in fixing the market value of the subject acquired lands and therefore, the Appeal fails.
18. Accordingly, this Appeal is dismissed.
No costs.
8 AKS, J & LNA, J 19.
As a sequel, Miscellaneous Petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
